question.text: What is reckless driving, and does it require intent?

answer.text: Reckless driving means operating a vehicle in a way that endangers people or property, whether or not it is intentional.

teaching.text: Reckless driving is about the danger created, whether or not you meant it. Remember: danger, not intent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reckless driving means operating a vehicle in a way that endangers people or property, whether or not it is intentional.

question.text: What can a reckless driving conviction add to your record?

answer.text: If an officer sees your driving as endangering a person or property, including another vehicle, you can be charged under the reckless driving statute and face up to eight points on your record if convicted.

teaching.text: A reckless driving conviction can add up to eight points. Remember: reckless means heavy points.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If an officer sees your driving as endangering a person or property, including another vehicle, you can be charged under the reckless driving statute and face up to eight points on your record if convicted.

question.text: When can tailgating or running a red light be treated as aggressive driving?

answer.text: Tailgating, passing on the shoulder or running a red light can be treated as aggressive when an officer believes it was willful and endangered others, and so can a mix of speeding, cutting off, swerving, honking, flashing lights, yelling and rude gestures.

teaching.text: Tailgating, shoulder passing and red-light running can count as aggressive when willful and endangering. Remember: willful danger is aggressive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tailgating, passing on the shoulder or running a red light can be treated as aggressive when an officer believes it was willful and endangered others, and so can a mix of speeding, cutting off, swerving, honking, flashing lights, yelling and rude gestures.

question.text: How does reckless driving differ from aggressive driving?

answer.text: Reckless driving needs no intent, only danger to people or property, while aggressive driving turns on willful acts that put others in danger.

teaching.text: Reckless needs no intent; aggressive turns on willful acts. Remember: reckless any, aggressive willful.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reckless driving needs no intent, only danger to people or property, while aggressive driving turns on willful acts that put others in danger.

question.text: Which acts toward another motorist can bring criminal charges beyond reckless driving?

answer.text: Showing a weapon to another motorist, bumping or ramming a vehicle, or chasing a vehicle at high speed can bring criminal charges beyond reckless driving.

teaching.text: Showing a weapon, ramming or chasing another vehicle can bring criminal charges. Remember: weapons and ramming are crimes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Showing a weapon to another motorist, bumping or ramming a vehicle, or chasing a vehicle at high speed can bring criminal charges beyond reckless driving.

question.text: How should you protect yourself from an aggressive driver?

answer.text: To protect yourself from an aggressive driver, do not engage: avoid eye contact, do not respond in kind, back off and let the driver go.

teaching.text: Avoid eye contact, do not respond, back off and let them go; afterward, report the driver to the free State Patrol cellphone line. Remember: do not engage.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To protect yourself from an aggressive driver, do not engage: avoid eye contact, do not respond in kind, back off and let the driver go.

question.text: What are warning signs that you may be becoming an aggressive driver?

answer.text: Anyone can become an aggressive driver; warning signs include insulting other drivers, blocking merges or passing, tailgating to push someone, angry speeding, running controls out of anger, honking or yelling, gestures, pursuing or ramming, getting out to confront, or thinking about attacking.

teaching.text: Insults, blocking, pushing, angry speeding and confrontation are warning signs of your own aggression. Remember: know your own warning signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone can become an aggressive driver; warning signs include insulting other drivers, blocking merges or passing, tailgating to push someone, angry speeding, running controls out of anger, honking or yelling, gestures, pursuing or ramming, getting out to confront, or thinking about attacking.

question.text: What does answering yes to a couple of the self-check questions mean?

answer.text: Answering yes to even a couple of the self-check questions means you may be at risk of becoming an aggressive driver.

teaching.text: Even a couple of yes answers on the self-check means you may be at risk. Remember: a couple yeses is risk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Answering yes to even a couple of the self-check questions means you may be at risk of becoming an aggressive driver.

question.text: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

answer.text: To avoid becoming aggressive, leave early, expect others to make mistakes, stay calm, keep anger from elsewhere out of your driving and let people merge even if they were rude.

teaching.text: Leave early, expect mistakes, stay calm and let people merge. Remember: leave early, stay calm.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid becoming aggressive, leave early, expect others to make mistakes, stay calm, keep anger from elsewhere out of your driving and let people merge even if they were rude.

question.text: When a crash seems likely, is there usually anything you can do?

answer.text: When a crash seems likely, many drivers panic, yet there is almost always something you can do to avoid it or lessen its results.

teaching.text: There is almost always something you can do to avoid or lessen a crash. Remember: never just panic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a crash seems likely, many drivers panic, yet there is almost always something you can do to avoid it or lessen its results.

question.text: What are the three ways to avoid a collision?

answer.text: The three ways to avoid a collision are to slow down or stop, to turn, or to speed up.

teaching.text: Slow down or stop, turn, or speed up. Remember: stop, turn, or speed up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The three ways to avoid a collision are to slow down or stop, to turn, or to speed up.

question.text: Is it usually faster to turn or to stop, and how should you steer around a hazard?

answer.text: You can usually turn a vehicle faster than you can stop it, so steer around a hazard if that will not cause another crash, gripping the wheel with both hands and staying ready to control the car afterward.

teaching.text: Turning is usually faster than stopping, so steer around when it is safe. Remember: turning beats stopping.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You can usually turn a vehicle faster than you can stop it, so steer around a hazard if that will not cause another crash, gripping the wheel with both hands and staying ready to control the car afterward.

question.text: Is leaving the road better or worse than a head-on collision?

answer.text: Leaving the road is generally a better outcome than a head-on collision with another vehicle.

teaching.text: Leaving the road is generally better than a head-on crash. Remember: off-road beats head-on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Leaving the road is generally a better outcome than a head-on collision with another vehicle.

question.text: When can accelerating be the way out of danger?

answer.text: Accelerating out of danger can be the answer when another vehicle is about to strike your side or rear and the road ahead is open; slow back down afterward.

teaching.text: With the road ahead open, accelerating can escape a side or rear impact. Remember: speed away when clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Accelerating out of danger can be the answer when another vehicle is about to strike your side or rear and the road ahead is open; slow back down afterward.

question.text: When and where should you watch most carefully for animals?

answer.text: Watch for animals especially in rural and mountain areas and between dusk and dawn, when about ninety percent of deer and elk crashes happen, and slow down and look on entering a marked animal crossing.

teaching.text: Watch for animals in rural and mountain areas, especially from dusk to dawn. Remember: dusk to dawn, watch for deer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Watch for animals especially in rural and mountain areas and between dusk and dawn, when about ninety percent of deer and elk crashes happen, and slow down and look on entering a marked animal crossing.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: dusk to dawn, watch for deer

question.text: Why might hitting a large animal be safer than swerving drastically?

answer.text: A drastic swerve to miss a large animal can cause loss of control and a worse crash, so hitting the animal may be the safest choice; focus on keeping control before, during and after impact.

teaching.text: A drastic swerve for a large animal can be worse than hitting it, so keep control. Remember: keep control, don't swerve.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A drastic swerve to miss a large animal can cause loss of control and a worse crash, so hitting the animal may be the safest choice; focus on keeping control before, during and after impact.

question.text: Which is more dangerous: swerving hard to miss a large animal or hitting it?

answer.text: Swerving hard to miss a large animal can be more dangerous than hitting it, and running off the road beats a head-on crash.

teaching.text: A hard swerve can be more dangerous than hitting the animal. Remember: swerving can be worse.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Swerving hard to miss a large animal can be more dangerous than hitting it, and running off the road beats a head-on crash.

question.text: How do you make an emergency stop with anti-lock brakes?

answer.text: To stop fast with anti-lock brakes, press hard and firmly and keep the pedal down even if it pushes back, since ABS works only while the pedal is pressed.

teaching.text: With ABS, press hard and keep the pedal down even when it pushes back. Remember: press hard and hold.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To stop fast with anti-lock brakes, press hard and firmly and keep the pedal down even if it pushes back, since ABS works only while the pedal is pressed.

question.text: How do you make an emergency stop without anti-lock brakes?

answer.text: To stop fast without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels; if they lock and you skid, ease off slightly, then brake again once the skid stops, repeating until stopped.

teaching.text: Without ABS, brake hard short of lockup, and ease off if the wheels lock. Remember: hard, short of lockup.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To stop fast without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels; if they lock and you skid, ease off slightly, then brake again once the skid stops, repeating until stopped.

question.text: How does emergency braking differ with and without ABS?

answer.text: Emergency braking is opposite by brake type: with ABS keep firm pressure and never let up, without ABS brake just short of lockup and ease off if you skid.

teaching.text: ABS means hold firm; no ABS means stop short of lockup. Remember: ABS hold, non-ABS ease.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Emergency braking is opposite by brake type: with ABS keep firm pressure and never let up, without ABS brake just short of lockup and ease off if you skid.

question.text: What do anti-lock brakes let you do while braking?

answer.text: Anti-lock brakes let you steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must turn and slow at once.

teaching.text: Anti-lock brakes let you steer while braking. Remember: ABS lets you steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anti-lock brakes let you steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must turn and slow at once.

question.text: How do you make an evasive turn without anti-lock brakes?

answer.text: Without anti-lock brakes, brake to slow somewhat, then release the brake before the evasive turn, and do not lock the front wheels or turn so sharply that the car only plows ahead.

teaching.text: Without ABS, brake, release, then make the evasive turn. Remember: brake, release, then turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without anti-lock brakes, brake to slow somewhat, then release the brake before the evasive turn, and do not lock the front wheels or turn so sharply that the car only plows ahead.

question.text: In what order do you brake and steer for an evasive turn without ABS?

answer.text: Without ABS, an emergency turn is done in sequence: brake to slow, release the brake, then steer away, never locking the front wheels.

teaching.text: Brake to slow, release, then steer, never locking the front wheels. Remember: slow, release, steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without ABS, an emergency turn is done in sequence: brake to slow, release the brake, then steer away, never locking the front wheels.

question.text: What greatly reduces the chance of a vehicle failure?

answer.text: Following the maintenance schedule in the owner's manual greatly reduces the chance of a vehicle failure.

teaching.text: Following the maintenance schedule greatly cuts the chance of failure. Remember: follow the maintenance schedule.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Following the maintenance schedule in the owner's manual greatly reduces the chance of a vehicle failure.

question.text: What should you do if your brakes fail?

answer.text: If the brakes fail, lift off the gas and pump the pedal; if that fails, apply the parking brake slowly, ready to release it if you skid, then shift to lower gears, find a safe spot off the road and do not drive on without brakes.

teaching.text: For brake failure, pump the pedal, then use the parking brake slowly and lower gears. Remember: pump, parking brake, downshift.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the brakes fail, lift off the gas and pump the pedal; if that fails, apply the parking brake slowly, ready to release it if you skid, then shift to lower gears, find a safe spot off the road and do not drive on without brakes.

question.text: What should you do if the gas pedal jams?

answer.text: If the gas pedal jams, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral quickly, pull off when safe and turn off the engine.

teaching.text: For a jammed gas pedal, shift to neutral, pull off and turn off the engine. Remember: jammed pedal, neutral.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the gas pedal jams, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral quickly, pull off when safe and turn off the engine.

question.text: How does the response to brake failure differ from a jammed gas pedal?

answer.text: Brake failure starts with pumping the pedal, then the parking brake applied slowly, then lower gears; a jammed gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral.

teaching.text: Pump for failed brakes; neutral for a jammed pedal. Remember: pump brakes, or neutral.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Brake failure starts with pumping the pedal, then the parking brake applied slowly, then lower gears; a jammed gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral.

question.text: What should you do in a tire blowout?

answer.text: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel tightly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas, brake lightly and slow gradually, then pull off the road somewhere safe.

teaching.text: In a blowout, hold straight, ease off the gas and brake lightly. Remember: hold straight, brake lightly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel tightly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas, brake lightly and slow gradually, then pull off the road somewhere safe.

question.text: Should you brake hard in a tire blowout?

answer.text: A blowout calls for gentle braking while holding straight, not hard braking or an immediate stop on the road.

teaching.text: Brake gently in a blowout, never hard. Remember: blowout means gentle braking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A blowout calls for gentle braking while holding straight, not hard braking or an immediate stop on the road.

question.text: What happens to steering and brakes if power fails, and what do you do?

answer.text: If power fails, hold the wheel firmly and pull off the road; steering will be hard but possible, and the brakes still work with much harder pressure.

teaching.text: Without power, steering and braking take much more effort but still work. Remember: hold firm, press harder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If power fails, hold the wheel firmly and pull off the road; steering will be hard but possible, and the brakes still work with much harder pressure.

question.text: What should you do if your headlights fail?

answer.text: If headlights fail, pull off as soon as possible, try the switch a few times, and if that does not work use the emergency flashers, turn signals or fog lights.

teaching.text: If headlights fail, pull off and use flashers, signals or fog lights. Remember: pull off, try flashers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If headlights fail, pull off as soon as possible, try the switch a few times, and if that does not work use the emergency flashers, turn signals or fog lights.

question.text: What must you show law enforcement after a crash?

answer.text: After a crash you must show proof of insurance to law enforcement, either at the scene or at the police station.

teaching.text: Show proof of insurance at the scene or the station. Remember: show insurance proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash you must show proof of insurance to law enforcement, either at the scene or at the police station.

question.text: Who must report an injury crash if the driver cannot?

answer.text: If the driver cannot physically report an injury crash, a passenger must report it and, if law enforcement directs, stay at the scene until officers arrive.

teaching.text: If the driver cannot report an injury crash, a passenger must. Remember: passenger reports for driver.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the driver cannot physically report an injury crash, a passenger must report it and, if law enforcement directs, stay at the scene until officers arrive.

question.text: What must you do after a crash?

answer.text: After a crash, stop at once and never leave, check for injuries and give reasonable help where practical, call law enforcement and emergency services, and exchange names, addresses, phone numbers, registration and insurance.

teaching.text: Stop, check injuries, help, call for help and exchange information. Remember: stop, help, call, exchange.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash, stop at once and never leave, check for injuries and give reasonable help where practical, call law enforcement and emergency services, and exchange names, addresses, phone numbers, registration and insurance.

question.text: What should you do if you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner?

answer.text: If you hit a parked car and cannot find its owner, call law enforcement and leave a note where the owner will find it.

teaching.text: For an unattended parked car, call law enforcement and leave a note. Remember: call police, leave a note.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you hit a parked car and cannot find its owner, call law enforcement and leave a note where the owner will find it.

question.text: What do drivers do in a qualifying crash during Accident Alert Status?

answer.text: During Accident Alert Status, when severe weather keeps officers from answering all crashes, drivers in a crash with no alcohol, drugs or injuries and drivable vehicles exchange information and must file a report within twenty-four hours.

teaching.text: Under Accident Alert Status, exchange information and report within twenty-four hours. Remember: exchange info, report later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During Accident Alert Status, when severe weather keeps officers from answering all crashes, drivers in a crash with no alcohol, drugs or injuries and drivable vehicles exchange information and must file a report within twenty-four hours.

question.text: What does the Move It Law require after a minor divided-highway crash?

answer.text: Under the Move It Law, after a minor divided-highway crash with drivable vehicles and no injuries, drugs or alcohol, drivers must get the vehicles off the highway, and police and insurers will not penalize them for it.

teaching.text: The Move It Law requires moving drivable cars off the highway after a minor crash. Remember: move drivable cars off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under the Move It Law, after a minor divided-highway crash with drivable vehicles and no injuries, drugs or alcohol, drivers must get the vehicles off the highway, and police and insurers will not penalize them for it.

question.text: How does the Move It Law differ from Accident Alert Status?

answer.text: The Move It Law moves drivable vehicles from a minor injury-free crash on a divided highway; under Accident Alert Status, drivers in a qualifying crash exchange information and file a report within twenty-four hours.

teaching.text: Move It clears the highway; Accident Alert means exchange and report later. Remember: move it versus report later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Move It Law moves drivable vehicles from a minor injury-free crash on a divided highway; under Accident Alert Status, drivers in a qualifying crash exchange information and file a report within twenty-four hours.

question.text: What does the Move Over Law require for a stopped vehicle with hazards flashing?

answer.text: The Move Over Law requires moving over one lane, when safe, for any stopped vehicle on a highway with hazards flashing; if that is unsafe or the road has one lane each way, slow to at least twenty miles per hour under the posted limit.

teaching.text: Move over a lane for stopped vehicles with hazards, or slow to twenty under the limit. Remember: move over or slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Move Over Law requires moving over one lane, when safe, for any stopped vehicle on a highway with hazards flashing; if that is unsafe or the road has one lane each way, slow to at least twenty miles per hour under the posted limit.

question.text: What are the two branches of the Move Over Law?

answer.text: The Move Over Law has two branches: change lanes when safe, or if you cannot, slow to at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

teaching.text: Change lanes when safe, otherwise slow down. Remember: change lanes or slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Move Over Law has two branches: change lanes when safe, or if you cannot, slow to at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

question.text: What do Good Samaritan laws expect, and how do they protect rescuers?

answer.text: Good Samaritan laws encourage helping in emergencies and expect common sense and reasonable skill within your training; acting as a reasonable, prudent person generally protects a rescuer from being sued and held financially responsible.

teaching.text: Reasonable, prudent rescuers are generally protected from being sued. Remember: reasonable help is protected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Good Samaritan laws encourage helping in emergencies and expect common sense and reasonable skill within your training; acting as a reasonable, prudent person generally protects a rescuer from being sued and held financially responsible.

question.text: How does a reasonable rescuer act at an emergency?

answer.text: A reasonable rescuer moves a victim only if life is in danger, asks a conscious victim before helping, checks for life-threatening problems first, calls for professional help and keeps giving care until trained help arrives.

teaching.text: Move a victim only if life is in danger, ask first, call for help and stay. Remember: ask, check, call, stay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A reasonable rescuer moves a victim only if life is in danger, asks a conscious victim before helping, checks for life-threatening problems first, calls for professional help and keeps giving care until trained help arrives.

question.text: What happens if you say yes to organ, eye and tissue donation when licensing?

answer.text: When applying for or renewing a license, permit or ID you are asked whether to register as an organ, eye and tissue donor; a yes puts a heart with a Y on the card and adds you to the Donate Life Colorado registry until you change it.

teaching.text: Saying yes adds a heart with a Y and puts you on the Donate Life Colorado registry. Remember: heart with a Y.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When applying for or renewing a license, permit or ID you are asked whether to register as an organ, eye and tissue donor; a yes puts a heart with a Y on the card and adds you to the Donate Life Colorado registry until you change it.

question.text: What is the voluntary gift you are asked about when licensing?

answer.text: You are also asked whether to make a voluntary gift to the organ and tissue donation awareness fund named for Emily Keyes and John W. Buckner, which pays for public outreach and education.

teaching.text: The voluntary gift funds organ and tissue donation outreach and education. Remember: gift funds donation awareness.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You are also asked whether to make a voluntary gift to the organ and tissue donation awareness fund named for Emily Keyes and John W. Buckner, which pays for public outreach and education.
